48a4b14c4a193313: Philadelphia workers who work for a private company with more than 10 employees may be entitled to paid sick leave. andresr/E+ Collection via Getty ImagesWhat do you do when you wake up with a runny nose and a cough? If you work in Philadelphia, you might have the legal right to a paid sick day. There is no federal right to paid sick leave. However, Philadelphia, like a growing number of states and cities nationwide, requires certain employers to provide paid time off when workers get sick. In Philadelphia, these requirements apply to private-sector employers with more than 10 employees. In theory, under these laws, sick workers have time to recover and avoid spreading germs, and they don’t have to choose between a sick day and a paycheck. For immigrant workers, though, it may not be that easy. I study restaurant work, an industry that depends on the labor of people who are foreign-born. Philadelphia’s award-winning dining scene wouldn’t be the same without the creativity and hard work of people from countries such as Mexico, Honduras and Guatemala. I studied this industry during the COVID-19 pandemic by working in a restaurant from 2021 to 2022, as well as by interviewing restaurant workers, managers and owners from 2021 to 2024. Some interviews were also conducted by my then-fellow Temple University graduate students Andrew Chelius and Camila Franco Rodríguez. Philadelphia’s paid sick leave law has been around since 2015. During the COVID-19 pandemic, federal and local laws temporarily expanded those protections. The Families First Coronavirus Response Act, a federal law which was passed on March 18, 2020, and amended by the CARES Act later that same month, required private-sector employers with less than 500 employees to provide 80 hours of paid sick time each year, on top of their existing paid leave policies, to full-time employees. A 2022 temporary expansion of the local paid sick leave law in Philadelphia, meanwhile, required private-sector employers with 25 or more employees to provide 40 hours of additional paid sick leave to eligible employees. What I found, though, was that several factors could make it hard for workers to take advantage of these policies. Immigrant workers faced unique, additional barriers. ‘$300 for a simple flu’ Our interviews and my immersion in restaurant work showed me that even during a pandemic, restaurant workers had to deal with employers skirting the law or misunderstanding policies. Workers were also impacted by long-standing service industry norms that discourage calling in sick, even when they’re under the weather. Many bosses required doctor’s notes, too, before they paid out any sick time – as I heard from bosses themselves. The local law says, however, that employers may require “reasonable documentation” – but only after an absence of more than two days. Immigrant workers, meanwhile, experienced additional hurdles. Take the example of doctor’s notes. Seeing a doctor is more affordable when you have health insurance. If you’re an undocumented immigrant, getting health insurance is difficult and expensive. Undocumented people are not eligible for Medicaid and are excluded from the Affordable Care Act marketplace. Only a few states try to mend the gap by offering health insurance for low-income people ineligible for Medicaid. Pennsylvania is not one of them. Bill – a pseudonym, like the other participants’ names in this article – is originally from Mexico, and he was a server at an Italian restaurant in Philadelphia’s Center City during the pandemic. When he got sick, his attitude was: “Keep the money. Don’t pay me for sick days.” What kept Bill from claiming sick pay? His employer required him to turn in a doctor’s note before he could receive paid sick leave. However, Bill was undocumented and did not have health insurance. “I wasn’t going to go to the doctor and spend US$300-$400 for a simple flu,” he said. Gaps arise when restaurants have different policies for front-of-house workers, who interact with customers, than back-of-house workers, who staff the kitchen. Willie B. Thomas/DigitalVision Collection via Getty Images Different policies for back-of-house workers In the restaurant where I worked, meanwhile, it was harder for immigrant workers to get sick days than nonimmigrant workers, based on my observations and interviews. This was not necessarily due to ill will toward immigrant workers. But there was a stricter policy around paid sick leave in the kitchen, which was staffed mostly by immigrants from Latin America. The chef who managed the kitchen described his policy like this: “If you bring me proof that you went to the doctor, and the doctor gave you a day or two days of rest, OK, that’s fine.” Those days would be paid. In the customer-facing front of the house, though, where a different manager was in charge, workers – including me – weren’t told they needed proof. These workers were almost all nonimmigrants and mostly white. I heard from Socorro, a prep cook who worked at a different restaurant, that managers where she worked were stingier with sick days for kitchen workers than for servers. “The servers were given their sick leave days and paid them. They’d say, ‘Oh no, my head hurts. I’m not going to work.’ But we couldn’t. ‘Oh, your head hurts? You have to put up with it and come to work.” In that workplace, Socorro said, immigrants also mainly worked in the kitchen, while servers were mostly U.S.-born. Fear of retaliation Immigrant workers in Philadelphia restaurants – both those with and without legal status – also weighed the risks they could face if they asked for paid sick days. These were not risks their nonimmigrant co-workers generally worried about. Claudia, a restaurant worker from Mexico, worked with a local organization called El Comité de Trabajadorxs de Restaurante – the Committee of Restaurant Workers – to educate her peers about paid sick leave. She found that immigrants were really scared of losing their jobs if they spoke up for themselves. “The majority – 80% if not 90% – even if they know they have paid sick hours … they don’t ask for it,” she said. “They don’t claim it, because [they think], ‘Oh, I am an immigrant and they are going to fire me.’ Or, 'Where am I going to get another job?’” Healthy workers, healthy public My research suggests that immigrants in Philadelphia face a gap between the promise and the reality of the city’s paid sick leave policies. These barriers might also help explain gaps in paid sick leave access between foreign-born and U.S.-born workers in other places that require it, like New York City or California. Gaps in access based on immigration status are an equity issue. But beyond that, research suggests that everyone wins if it’s easier for workers to get paid sick leave. Paid sick leave makes for healthier workers, and healthier workers make for a healthier public. 6a2137afaca073ec: Some Windows 11 applications might fail to install or launch after Microsoft's November hotpatch, but not to worry: there's a Registry tweak to work around it.
Microsoft has confirmed it isn't administrators' imaginations. The November hotpatch is causing application errors, including in little-used and obscure apps such as Outlook.

Affected applications may fail during installation, launch, or use, displaying errors such as "ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099)." Microsoft's investigation points to applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, msi.dll. The problem is more common with 32-bit software, but can also affect 64-bit applications "under certain circumstances."

The workaround involves fiddling with the Registry on affected devices, so is not for the faint of heart and a backup is a good idea before diving in. Microsoft says the key "HotPatchTableSize" in the folder "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" needs to be set to "2000" followed by a restart.
Just the thing to round out the week for administrators.

The issue affects the November hotpatch, not the standard monthly cumulative security update. "Devices which installed the November 2026 Windows monthly security update are not expected to be affected by this issue," Microsoft said.

Windows hotpatches are security updates that don't require a device restart (unless, as in this instance, administrators have to do so to address errors after a hotpatch is installed). Windows 11 hotpatching requires version 24H2 or later, an eligible subscription, and the necessary management and security configuration.

"Hotpatch update package size is significantly smaller than the standard cumulative updates," Microsoft said, and the goal is to "streamline the installation process and enhance compliance efficiency."
The offending hotpatch, KB5132043, was released on November 10. It followed the October 13 baseline, which was a prerequisite.
Microsoft made hotpatching the default in Windows Autopatch earlier this year. At the time, we asked: "What could possibly go wrong?"
Thanks to November's hotpatch, we have our answer. ®

e853741b74a166f4: Now that Ismail Lasim sudah buat pengakukan terbuka bahawa beliau tidak pernah letak jawatan menteri besar Negeri Sembilan, persoalan penting ialah siapa yang mengutus ‘surat peletakan jawatannya’ kepada Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan?
Persoalan ini amat penting kerana pada hemat saya pihak yang mengutus surat itu telah membohongi atau cuba membohongi Tuanku Muhriz Tuan Munawir.
Apa tidaknya kerana pihak itu telah memaklumkan perkara yang nampaknya tidak benar dan mahu baginda mempercayai isi kandungan surat itu mengenai peletakan jawatan menteri besar.

Orang atau orang-orang yang terlibat dengan penghantaran surat itu saya kira tidak sangka akan reaksi Yang Dipertuan Besar sebaik menerima surat itu. Atas kebijaksanaan Tuanku Muhriz, Istana Negeri Sembilan menegaskan (ketika itu) belum mengesahkan ketulenan surat itu meskipun menurut Setiausaha Agung BN Zambry Abdul Kadir ia telah ditandatangani Ismail.
Sebelum berbicara lanjut elok kita imbau kembali kenyataan Pengelola Bijaya Diraja Istana Negeri Sembilan Azizi Mohamad Ali yang dikeluarkan 17 Nov lalu berbunyi begini:
“Istana Negeri Sembilan mengambil maklum akan kenyataan Zambry Abdul Kadir, Setiausaha Agung Barisan Nasional berhubung peletakan jawatan Ismail Lasim sebagai menteri besar Negeri Sembilan.
Kenyataan itu dimuat naik di media sosial pada 10 malam 16 Nov dan kelihatan berdasarkan salinan surat peletakan jawatan yang berada dalam milikan beliau.
Surat peletakan itu telah dihantar ke Istana Hingap Seremban pada 12.16 pagi 17 November”.

Bagi saya ini amat janggal. Zambry telah menghebahkan ‘peletakan jawatan’ Ismail pada malam 16 Nov tetapi ‘surat peletakan jawatan’ Ismail dihantar ke Istana Hinggap hanya pada keesokan hari yakni 17 Nov.
Bukankah ini bermakna Zambry sudah mengumumkan peletakan jawatan Ismail long before Yang Dipertuan Besar dimaklumkan? Is this proper dalam urusan dengan istana?

Berbalik kenyataan Pengelola Bijya Diraja Istana Negeri Sembilan yang disebut tadi: “Surat itu diserahkan oleh seorang individu yang memperkenalkan dirinya sebagai Hamidi daripada firma guaman Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq"
Aneh. Jika saya mahu letak jawatan misalnya daripada syarikat tempat saya bekerja, saya akan umum sendiri my resignation. Bukan orang lain yang umum.
Dan surat peletakan jawatan akan saya serah sendiri kepada majikan bukan meminta pihak lain melakukannya.
Dalam kes ‘peletakan jawatan’ Ismail adakah ‘molek’ menyerahkan surat kepada Yang Dipertuan Besar menerusi third party? Dan tidak menghadap untuk mempersembahkan surat personally?

Ada lagi yang dihuraikan Pengelola Bijaya Diraja Istana Negeri Sembilan. Menurut beliau: “Pada jam 6.38 petang,semalam (16 Nov 2026 ) Setiausaha Sulit Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan telah menyampaikan kepada Ismail melalui aplikasi WhatsApp perkenan Tuanku Muhriz untuk menghadap seperti yang dipohon oleh menteri besar itu.
Perkara tu telah diakui terima oleh Ismail dan acara menghadap telah ditetapkan pada pukul 10 pagi Jumaat (20 Nov).
Perkenan untuk menghadap itu telah diberikan 80 minit lebih awal sebelum siaran media Zambry yang memaklumkan peletakan jawatan itu.
Aneh dan pelik. Ismail yang memohon menghadap bertindak ‘meneruskan hasrat letak jawatan’ (yang diumum Zambry) setelah tahu Yang Dipertuan Besar telah perkenankan permohonannya?

Berbalik pula kepada kenyataan setiausaha agung BN itu. Kata Zambry pengerusi gabungan itu Zahid Hamidi sudah menerima salinan suara peletakan jawatan Ismail yang diutuskan kepada Yang Dipertuan Besar.

“Pengerusi Barisan Nasional akan mengemukakan cadangan calon menteri besar yang baharu untuk dipersembahkan ke hadapan Duli Yang Maha Mulia Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilsn selaras dengan peruntukan Undang Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan”.

Zahid insisted Ismail resigned voluntarily. Beliau juga memberitahu media hanya satu nama akan dipersembahkan. Ini menurut saya tidak beri Yang Dipertuan Besar banyak pilihan. Atau tidak beri pilihan langsung.

Apa pun itu sudah tidak terpakai kerana hari ini Yang Dipertuan Besar bertitah supaya Ismail teruskan tugas sebagai menteri besar. Ini kata Ismail pada sidang medianya selepas menghadap Tuanku Muhriz.
Saya ulangi apa kata Ismail pada sidang media itu “Saya tak pernah setuju surat ini dihantar dan saya pun tak hantar sendiri surat ini kepada Tuanku. Saya hanya tahu melalui media sosial.”
Namun Ismail mengaku surat peletakan jawatan semenagnya ada dalam simpanan pimpinan parti namun tidak dinyatakan sebabnya.
Setahu saya ada parti mewajibkan Ahli Parlimen dan Adun yang mewaklinya menandatangnai surat melepaskan jawatan atau kedudukan dalam usaha memastkan mereka tidak lompat parti.
The pre signed resignation letter will be released in the event of crossing over to other parties. Ini amalan lazim sebelum ada anti hopping law.
Bagaimanapun boleh dirumuskan penjelasan Ismail diterima Yang Dipertuan Besar pada upacara menghadap semalam. Lantas baginda mahu Ismail kekal sebagai menteri besar.
Bagi saya episod Negeri Sembilan tamparan hebat kepada BN khususnya Umno yang selama ini megah mendakwa ia mempertahakan Raja-Raja Melayu dn kedaulatan Istana.
Di Negeri Sembilan tidak boleh dinafikan Umno mendekati (bersekongkol?) kumpulan yang cuba menurunkan Tuanku Muhriz daripada takhta dan gagal.
Kesimpulan terbaik saya kira dibuat oleh Naib Pengerusi DAP Syahredzan Johan “Semua tindakan ini adalah berasaskan suatu perkara yang terbukti tidak benar. Ismail Lasim tidak pernah letak jawatan.”
Adakah Umno cuba untuk memperdayakan Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan dan rakyat dalam hal ini?
Nota kaki: Terbaharu, lewat petang ini Azizi mengeluarkan kenyatan menyatakan Ismail perlu menunjukkan beliau mendapat sokongan majoriti Adun untuk terus memegang jawatan menteri besar.
Kenyataan itu juga berkata tidak tepat dan tidak berdasarkan fakta untuk mengatakan Istana mahu Ismail kekal sebagai menteri besar memandangkan beliau sendiri menegaskan tidak meletakkan jawatan.
Menurutnya, pihak Istana akan mematuhi sepenuhnya konvensyen dan peruntukan perlembagaan.

2b876ce610b840bc: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
What we learned when our Roundtables explored the quest to make minds immortal

To preserve our sense of self, some scientists are working on ways to keep our brains going—even beyond death. In their quest for cognitive immortality, these “mind savers” are exploring everything from head transplants and brain freezing to conscious software avatars.

In the latest MIT Technology Review Roundtables event, senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado joined science editor Mary Beth Griggs to examine these ideas. After following the money, the science, and the philosophy, he came back part skeptical, part awestruck. Here’s a taste of what Antonio found—and what he made of it.

Not all the projects are quite what they seem: A $190 million US government program to develop replacement brain tissue is officially about treating stroke, but “it’s also a fig leaf for the actual ambition”: living forever.

AI could lead to convincing mind clones: Large language models are making it possible to build AI copies of people that act quite like the real thing. “This digital avatar might not be good enough for you, but what if it’s good enough for me?”
Immortality can be a hard sell: One company, Nectome, wants to preserve brains within 12 minutes of medically assisted death. “If you’re selling a hot product, this is not it.”
It’s not always clear what we’re trying to preserve: “I’m not even sure that I have a very good claim to be myself.”
There’s an upside to life as a brain in a jar: “You can surf the internet. I do that pretty much 12 hours a day, anyway.”
To find out which of these ideas might actually work, subscribers can now watch the full conversation on demand.

54cd77410d7416bf: BANGKOK, Nov 20 — The top UN court’s ruling on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide repeatedly name-checked one man — Min Aung Hlaing, the country’s president who, as a general, led the military during the campaign against the Rohingya.

The International Court of Justice’s findings concerned state culpability, not individual guilt over the Myanmar military’s campaign of rape and killings against the mostly Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017.
But Min Aung Hlaing was called out for his speeches against the Rohingya while armed forces chief during the so-called “clearance operations” in western Rakhine state.
“The court considers that the Senior General’s messages, as reported, were capable of fuelling hatred against the Rohingya,” the ruling said.
It said he repeatedly portrayed them as “a violent threat to other ethnic groups that needed to be addressed”.
He gave speeches during the violence praising the security forces’ “brilliant efforts” and referring to “‘solving’ the ‘unfinished job’ of the ‘Bengali problem’,” the court said.
Min Aung Hlaing took power in a 2021 coup and was installed as civilian president this April. Since then, he has embarked on a tour of regional capitals in a bid for international recognition.
The court had “made him the most prominent agent of the genocide”, said independent Myanmar analyst David Mathieson.
“By naming him several times, it definitely puts him even further in the crosshairs than he already was.”
Richard Horsey, senior Asia adviser at the International Crisis Group, noted the ruling was not against Min Aung Hlaing personally.
“But he commanded the military during the 2017 operations, and he is now the head of a state found responsible for genocide,” Horsey told AFP via email.
He did not expect it to stop the leader travelling, but it would “make his effort to be accepted as a normal head of state harder”, he said.
“Any government that receives him will now be asked about it.”
‘Legal exposure’
The UN court’s decisions are binding and cannot be appealed, but it has no way of enforcing its verdicts.
Min Aung Hlaing’s “more serious legal exposure lies elsewhere”, said Horsey.
In 2024, the chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, also based in The Hague, asked judges for an arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing over alleged crimes against humanity.
A case is also underway in Argentina under the principle of universal jurisdiction — the idea that some crimes are so heinous they can be heard in any court.
The bespectacled Min Aung Hlaing became armed forces head in 2011, just as Myanmar broke with its history of iron-fisted martial rule and began an experiment with democracy.
He spent a decade jostling with civilian leaders, playing second fiddle to Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, the nation’s internationally feted campaigner for popular rule.

Suu Kyi addressed the International Court of Justice at a hearing in 2019, saying the case risked reigniting the crisis that led to the Rohingya’s expulsion and said there was no “genocidal intent” behind the crackdown.
She was accused of defending the generals, leaving her international reputation in tatters. She was not mentioned in the verdict.
Myanmar has always denied genocide, arguing that its actions targeted a military uprising from insurgents after a series of attacks left a dozen security personnel dead.
Min Aung Hlaing has always steadfastly rejected allegations of human rights abuses.
But he was sanctioned after the violence against the Rohingya by the United States over what Washington called “ethnic cleansing”.
He was further sanctioned and Myanmar widely shunned after he led the coup just months away from mandatory retirement.
The putsch triggered a civil war that conflict monitor ACLED estimates has killed more than 100,000 people on all sides. — AFP
fc802768927fd20b: PORTIMAO, Nov 20 — Marc Marquez has a date with history this weekend when he can retain his MotoGP crown at the Portuguese Grand Prix and in the process claim a record-equalling eighth world title in the premier class of motorcycling, 13 years after his first.

Just 14 points from the final two race weekends, in Portimao and then Valencia, will be enough for Ducati’s Marquez to draw level with Giacomo Agostini, who won his 500cc championships between 1966 and 1975.

Marquez could seal the deal as early as Saturday if he wins the sprint race, but with a 60-point gap separating him from his closest rival and compatriot Jorge Martin, it would need a total disaster for him to not finish top of the pile come the end of next weekend in Spain.
Marco Bezzecchi is still technically in the fight but, trailing by 74, the Italian needs maximum points from Portimao and Marquez to not score any in order to stay in it.
“It’s true that we are in a very good situation but in MotoGP everything can happen... We have many different moments over a race weekend,” said Marquez on Thursday.
“I have a number in my mind which is 14, 14 points. If I achieve 14 points in the next two weekends, this weekend and Valencia, it doesn’t matter what the others do.”
Marquez’s record in the sprint races gives him a good chance of heading into Sunday’s GP already the 2026 champion, with 10 wins and four podiums this year.

That’s in comparison with seven wins and one other podium finish in the actual GPs, in a year in which he hasn’t dominated quite like he did last season when he won his first title in six years with five rounds remaining.
Ducati has been a happy home for Marquez who has returned to top form in the last two years, following a long recovery from a broken arm suffered at the start of the 2020 season.

He moved up to the factory team from Gresini at the start of last year and took the reins as principal rider from two-time world champion Francesco Bagnaia, a disciple of Marquez’s great rival Valentino Rossi who also has seven MotoGP titles.
The difference between the pair has been stark, with Bagnaia languishing ninth in the riders’ championship and scuttling off to join Bezzecchi at Aprilia next season.

Marquez became the youngest ever MotoGP champion in his debut season in 2013 and then went on to win the title in five of the next six seasons, and he wants to make up for the time he lost to injury as he heads into his mid-30s.
“The life of an athlete is short so you need to take the maximum,” said Marquez.
“The fastest Marc was 2013. 2013, or maybe 2019. The best Marc is now, 100 percent. I would have liked to have the mentality I have now at 20 years old.”
Marquez will get his weekend underway on Friday with two practice sessions, at 1045GMT and 1500GMT. — AFP
5a4cb3e0a0e44110: AKANDA (Gabon), Nov 20 — Low tide and blue skies made for ideal razor clamming conditions on Gabon’s coasts where gastronome-on-tour Kwame Asie was on hand to document the local fisherwomen’s culinary traditions.

Armed with the latest smartphone and camera, the 32-year-old Nigerian-Ghanaian influencer and chef followed the barefoot villagers’ every move on the beach, ready to share their know-how with his 50,000 or so followers.
A self-described “food archivist” and “gastro-diplomat”, Asie is on a mission to catalogue the whole of Africa’s food heritage through a mixed grill of gastronomy, anthropology and geography.
“The work I do is trying to bridge the gap between west Africa, central Africa, even east Africa,” Asie told AFP on the beach at Cap Esterias, on the outskirts of the Gabonese capital, Libreville.
“Food is identity for us as Africans, food creates memory, food is the way we express our tradition,” he added.
“If this knowledge goes away without it being preserved, it becomes a problem of not being able to identify culture and what it means for us.”
Nearby, the fisherwomen of the Lambi La Mbocka cooperative tracked their prospective haul’s tell-tale traces in the still-wet sand.
“Come look, they’re calling you over there to see something incredible,” one of them shouted to Asie with a laugh.
Today’s discovery: a sea snail halfway through savouring a clam.
‘Our roots’
Asie himself was fishing for the women’s knowledge of the local razor clams, sea snails, oysters and other seafood — all delicacies for the Benga people of coastal Gabon.
“The razor clam is Benga heritage. It’s part of our roots,” said Stella Ehebo Eyavo, a member of the cooperative.
Asie explained that his work “is really to understand Indigenous cuisine”.

“The Atlantic feeds a lot of people that live close to the water, and to understand their food you need to understand their environment, their ecology as well,” he added, gazing out towards the deep blue ocean.
After the clamming came the cooking.
Once the razor clams are shelled, the women wash the off-white flesh to prepare what the Benga call the “mehenenes” — a matter of national pride in Gabon.
By asking questions and filming, Asie hopes to use his decade-long experience as a chef to teach his audience about Africa’s specialties — without the local gastronomy becoming lost in translation.
“When you translate to a language like English, for example, a lot of information (is) being lost, so it’s very important that (this) information (is) being stored in the actual language,” he said.
‘One big kitchen’
“I think it’s important for us to be able to document our food. Most of our African techniques or food ingredients are not documented,” he said.
Most of that knowledge is passed down by word-of-mouth and “stays in the Indigenous community”, he warned.
“This is information we need to pass on to the next generation.”
The chef emphasised that “food is not just nutrition”, pointing out that African food could have ceremonial, medicinal or even religious significance.

“Where I come from, for example, if a woman (gives birth and is) put to bed there’s a food you cook for her to eat to heal her bowels, if a man is getting married there’s food you eat, if a man is about to serve his god there (is) food that you cook for the gods as well.”
To achieve his ambition of bringing Africans together through cooking, Asie has embarked on an Africa-wide tour, with the hope of completing all 54 of the continent’s countries in three years’ time.
After having criss-crossed all of west Africa — tasting Liberian cassava leaves, Sierra Leonean fish balls and Senegal’s rice thieb along the way — the chef’s next stop is the continent’s centre.
“I feel like Africa is one big kitchen,” Asie said.
“I say that because we are much more similar than we know.” — AFP
35d924813e8f8450: Global consultancy PwC says IT departments struggling to secure funding for ERP upgrades should make the expected benefits of AI part of their pitch.

The Oracle and SAP mega-partner told El Reg that a "clean core" – modern enterprise applications with fewer customizations embedded in the underlying system – makes deploying AI agents easier. Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration.

Oracle and SAP are both trying to persuade customers to move from established ERP systems to newer platforms. For SAP, that means S/4HANA, preferably in the cloud. For Oracle, it means Fusion Cloud Applications. Moving from ECC or E-Business Suite, respectively, can involve root-and-branch changes to technology and business processes, rather than a straightforward software upgrade.

Thousands of organizations still rely on these aging, often heavily customized systems. IT leaders struggle to justify a costly, time-consuming migration when the reward appears to be doing the same meat-and-veg business processes slightly better. For example, a survey of SAP users last year found that 95 percent said building a positive case for migration required substantial effort or was genuinely challenging.

Speaking to The Register, Jennifer Colapietro, PwC digital core modernization platform leader, said: "You're seeing it a lot more as part of the rationale for the business case for why they should upgrade, answering the question: 'Why now? What should we prioritize?' Certainly, AI and getting the value of AI, a key business case justification for that.

"Folks have budgets for ERP, but now [funding for transformation is] being split because they also have budgets for AI. But there's synergies across them. If you look at moving to a clean digital core ERP, that will help them to realize the AI value faster... be able to turn on AI and be able to start to automate a lot of the processes and implement the agents. That helps to build the business case."

SAP recently introduced Joule 2.0 while Oracle has announced Fusion Claw. With both of these new technologies, the vendors are promising customers they can build AI agents to automate business processes and perform some work that was previously done by humans. Colapietro argued that moving to more modern platforms makes deploying AI agents easier and more effective than adding AI capabilities around legacy systems.

"It is more challenging to apply AI to the older systems. We focus on the importance of a clean digital core as the foundation for getting the value and effectiveness out of AI and scaling AI responsibly. I think that's given," she said.

An ERP replacement isn't the only route to AI, however. European home improvement retailer Kingfisher – which owns the B&Q brand in the UK – eschewed SAP's overtures to upgrade its ECC system, despite encroaching deadlines. Mainstream maintenance for supported ECC 6.0 versions ends in December 2027, with optional extended maintenance through 2030 at a premium of two percentage points on the existing maintenance base.
Kingfisher opted instead for third-party support from Rimini Street, building an AI strategy around its existing ERP system using a combination of technology from Databricks and Google.
AI might help sell an ERP migration to the board. It doesn't make replacing the ERP system a prerequisite. ®

90752f7c49cc9934: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN), rejecting the Home Office's argument that acknowledging its existence would damage national security.
The order has been widely reported as demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data.
The three judges pointed to extensive public reporting, statements by US officials, and media briefings they concluded had been authorized by the UK government.
The Home Office had previously adopted its "neither confirm nor deny" (NCND) policy, as is standard when discussing national security matters.
The story broke in February 2025, when The Washington Post reported that the Home Office had demanded an iCloud backdoor the previous month.

A TCN is a notice issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, which compels recipients, such as tech companies, to implement technical changes that facilitate the UK government's legal surveillance powers.

For Apple, a company that has long made privacy central to its marketing, and famously rejected an FBI order to break open an iPhone to assist a terror probe, being served the TCN meant it either had to somehow defy a legal order issued by the UK, or undermine the encryption technology that customers expected.

While it remained officially unconfirmed at the time, Apple's decision to revoke Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for UK users in February 2025 was widely interpreted as indirect confirmation of the demand.

At the same time, US policymakers urged then-director of national intelligence Tulsi Gabbard to oppose the UK's demands under the assumption that they also sought to backdoor Apple's data in a way that would affect US citizens.
In August 2025, Gabbard announced that the UK had agreed to drop its demand for access to Americans' encrypted data. ADP is still available to users in the US.

Apple's ADP extends end-to-end encryption to additional categories of iCloud data, including backups, photos, and notes. Only trusted devices retain access to the relevant encryption keys, leaving Apple unable to decrypt that protected content for investigators.

Without ADP, those additional categories revert to standard protection: the data remains encrypted, but Apple holds the keys and can disclose content in response to valid legal demands. Some categories remain end-to-end encrypted regardless.
Apple has an explainer on what data types remain end-to-end encrypted, even without ADP enabled, and those that are not.
What the judgment does not confirm
While the IPT's judgment confirms that the Home Office served Apple with a TCN, judges have yet to decide whether key details about the case can be made public.

"Although there has been extensive media coverage and public statements about the existence of a technical capability notice, there has been no publication of its precise content," the judgment stated. "All parties recognize that there may be matters of detail that must be kept secret in order to preserve national security and the public interest.

"We agree that it would be damaging to national security if all of the material (including the content of the technical capability evidence, and the evidence of Apple and the respondent) were publicly disclosed.

"That does not mean every detail must be kept secret in order to preserve national security. There may be some information that could be disclosed publicly without damaging national security. It is not, however, practical to determine the precise boundaries now."
The parties are working toward a substantive hearing in the first half of 2027. Apple's first challenge was dismissed following a "change in circumstances," and it filed a second claim in July 2026.
The Financial Times reported in October 2025 that the UK had replaced its original notice with a new order focused on British users.
The proceedings also include a separate challenge to the TCN regime brought by Liberty, Privacy International, and two individuals.

A government spokesperson said: "Terrorists, child abusers and organized crime groups cannot be allowed to operate beyond the reach of the law. The right to privacy is crucial but it should not come at the expense of the safety of the British public.

"A judge can authorize access to a criminal's home, a parcel they've sent, or a car they drive. The online world is no different. These powers are subject to strict safeguards and the government never has direct access to a company's communications systems or data.

"Apple has been helping the police and intelligence agencies pursue criminals and bring them to justice for several years, in accordance with the law. This Technical Capability Notice simply requires that they maintain the ability to do so.
"Decisions affecting the safety of the British public must be made by democratically elected governments and independent judges, not in the boardrooms of technology companies."
Apple did not immediately respond to our request for comment. ®

b6f28c6c829ce1b8: A Windows 11 passkey bug can leave Android phones announcing that authentication failed even when it succeeded. Microsoft has now released a fix for versions 25H2 and 26H2.

The problem occurs when users sign in on a Windows 11 PC using a passkey stored on an Android phone. Scan the QR code, and the Android device might display the message: "Something went wrong. Restart the process on your other device and try again."

Except it might not have gone wrong at all. Microsoft's guidance explains: "In cases where authentication completes successfully on the Windows device, the error message on the Android device is not supposed to appear and can be safely ignored."

Cross-device authentication lets users sign in on one device using a passkey held on another, without typing a password or copying a verification code. Microsoft says the issue affects operations using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, and can occur in Edge or Chrome – not just when signing in through Microsoft Entra ID.
Cross-device passkey operations with an iPhone aren't affected.
An authentication system that cries failure after a successful sign-in isn't doing much for user confidence. Nor will it endear itself to support teams fielding the resulting tickets.

Microsoft has included a fix in KB5132057, the optional non-security preview update released on November 19 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. Until affected devices are patched, users can ignore the Android error if authentication has completed successfully on the PC. ®

32f5e0f71df79564: SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — An unprecedented summit between Chinese, US and Russian leaders this week in Shenzhen was light on substance but immensely symbolic, analysts say.
From nuclear weapons to reforming the United Nations and cancelling international arrest warrants, AFP looks at what was announced, its significance and what might come next:
Substance or hot air?
The three leaders jointly declared lofty goals to “reduce nuclear risks” and reform the United Nations, as well as commitments to immunity for state officials.
Their “Declaration toward Peace” also said the countries plan to boost oil supply and reaffirmed the importance of “stable energy flows”.

The promise of dialogue on nuclear risks and non-proliferation “creates an opening for cooperation despite disagreements over arsenal reductions”, said Sun Chenghao, senior fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University.
“Implementation is now the main test,” he told AFP.
Progress could be signalled by dates for nuclear talks or the appointment of designated officials.
Beijing previously rebuffed Trump’s invitations to nuclear arms talks, arguing the US and Russia should first cut their giant arsenals before it agreed to discuss its smaller stockpiles.
The four-point declaration contains few details on future actions, with Germany’s Chancellor Friedrich Merz calling the meeting a “photo op”.
The “fairly sparse” points were “least common denominators” among the leaders, said Ryan Hass at the Brookings Institution.
Trump told reporters he would give a press conference on Friday, where he may provide more details.
A new Yalta?

The symbolism of three powerful leaders gathering to discuss global security issues — including Putin’s invasion of Ukraine and Trump’s war with Iran — had raised comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference.
Then-leaders of Britain, the United States and the Soviet Union met to hash out the post-World War II settlement and re-draw European borders.
Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky and European powers worried Thursday’s summit would push for a peace settlement favourable to Moscow without them at the table.

The format “suggests the creation of conditions where Beijing, Moscow, and Washington call the shots for the rest of the world”, said Chong Ja Ian, an associate professor at the National University of Singapore.
But “a functioning ‘G3’ would require much greater agreement among the three countries and cooperation from many other governments,” Tsinghua University’s Sun told AFP.
“The Yalta analogy also overlooks today’s economic interdependence and the influence of regional actors,” he said.
Should Europe, others worry?
Other US allies such as Japan, South Korea and Taiwan — which unlike China and Russia are vibrant democracies — will also have eyed the summit with unease.

“From South Korea’s perspective, this inevitably raises questions about whether it can continue to rely on its alliance with the United States,” said Lee Jae-mook, a political science professor at Hankuk University of Foreign Studies.
“The pillars of South Korea’s foreign and security policy that it has long taken for granted are being shaken,” Lee told AFP.
Japan, too, may reconsider its relationships with China and the US.

“If China and Russia really draw the United States together, I think Japan will have a huge pressure to... make a better relationship with China,” said Tzeng Wei-feng, an associate research fellow at Taiwan’s National Chengchi University.
However, Tokyo and Washington maintain a bilateral defense pact, so there will likely be “no substantial change” in their ties, he added.
The US has roughly 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan — whose relations with China are poor — and 28,500 in South Korea.
Despite the bonhomie between Xi, Trump and Putin displayed in Shenzhen, major strategic differences remain between their countries.
Washington has curbed Beijing’s access to US technologies, while Moscow is fighting a Ukraine that still relies in large part on American intelligence.
Diverging national interests between China, the US and Russia means the rest of Asia won’t be “overly concerned” yet, according to Dylan Loh of Singpaore’s Nanyang Technological University.
The format may not stick, especially after Trump leaves office in two years, he said.
What next?
“Perhaps the most noteworthy aspect is the absence of any commitment to reconvene or continue meeting at the leader-level,” said Brookings’ Hass.

With no follow-up announced, eyes will turn to next month’s G20 summit in Miami, where Xi and Trump are due to hold their fourth meeting of the year, and Putin could make his first appearance at the grouping since his war in Ukraine began.
He has been shunned by most Western leaders since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.
Still, “there is little chance that such a meeting will be held again”, said Shen Dingli, a Shanghai-based scholar of international relations.

International Criminal Court (ICC) members — which exclude the US — are obliged to detain Putin if he travels to their territory after the court issued a warrant for him for war crimes associated with the Ukraine invasion.

“Putin has been ruled an international criminal by the ICC, and most APEC and G20 members are signatories to the Rome Statute. So, there are few opportunities for the three countries’ leaders to convene,” said Shen. — AFP

a65db3693b54f7f2: BRUSSELS, Nov 20 — UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit.
But in a potential spoiler for Burnham’s “reset”, Brussels said the deals coming into force would be conditional on reaching an agreement to cut university fees for EU students in Britain.
Since taking power this summer, the prime minister has smashed through the taboos in Britain’s toxic debate over relations with Europe — going as far as to float rejoining the bloc one day.

For now the summit with EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa will focus on much smaller steps to help turn the page a decade after the UK voted to leave — while Burnham saves for later the bigger decisions on what could come next.

“Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighbourhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe,” a statement from Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.
On the table in Brussels are three main agreements: a deal cutting red tape for food exports, another linking the two sides’ emissions-trading schemes and a third on a “youth experience scheme”.
Burnham argues those moves — which were in the pipeline long before he entered Downing Street — will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted.
British firms will export to Europe more easily again and 100,000 under-30s from each side will be allowed to reside for up to three years in each other’s territory for work, study or travel.
But while the mood music at the meeting may be much improved, old habits still die hard.
Brussels and London wrangled ferociously down to the wire over the details.

One key sticking point was on pinning London down to a future agreement on cutting fees for EU students at UK universities to the level paid by their British counterparts — with the EU making the other details entering into force contingent on striking a deal.

“We have not yet reached an agreement on tuition fees and we have given ourselves six months to reach that agreement,” said an EU official, adding that the three core deals would be signed “in parallel” with those talks.
‘Tread carefully’
The big question that the Brussels meeting won’t answer is what Burnham plans next.
“After the summit, we will initiate a discussion with our EU partners about options for our long-term relationship,” Burnham said earlier this week.

Having previously said he’d like to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime, the former Manchester mayor has promised to lay out options that could range from leaving things as they are to entering the customs union or becoming a member again.
The strategy is in part because polls now regularly indicate most Britons regret Brexit and would vote to re-enter the bloc if a referendum was held tomorrow.
It is also reflective of Britain’s weak economy, damaged by Brexit, and how much the world has changed since 2016, with Europe firmly behind Ukraine in its war against Russian aggression.
Burnham hopes friendlier EU relations will help build a broad centre-left coalition to win the next general election, not anticipated until 2029.
But the strategy comes with huge risks, not least because his own party — never mind the country — is divided on how to proceed.
For now, the prime minister appears to have tempered his early urgency.
“I’m happy with closer ties but he does need to tread carefully,” one Labour MP told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity.

Burnham’s push leaves him open to accusations of Brexit betrayal from the opposition Conservatives and hard-right Reform UK party of Nigel Farage — who will give his own press conference in Brussels Friday.
In Brussels meanwhile, there is little expectation the UK will return to the fold any time soon.
“I doubt he’d take the risk of a major step that would be so radioactive,” said one senior EU diplomat.
“He’ll probably keep on trying to nibble away around the edges to improve ties — and we are open to have as close a relationship as possible.” — AFP
3ded48973ec92db0: SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — A man who impersonated an Aide-de-Camp (ADC) to the Raja Muda of Selangor and had been sentenced to imprisonment for fraud involving property and luxury vehicle purchases was sentenced to another 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane today for similar offences.

Today, Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, was sentenced by the Magistrate’s Court here to a total of 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane for cheating two victims of RM73,000 in a vehicle auction scam.
Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin meted out the jail sentence and fine after Al Zulfadly pleaded guilty to the charges.
The court ordered the prison terms to run consecutively, effective from the dates he was charged with the offences.
Meanwhile, Al Zulfadly’s fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty to the same charges. The court fixed Jan 19, 2027, for mention.
Today’s proceedings focused on the presentation of facts in Al Zulfadly’s case and the sentencing.

The couple was accused of conspiring with a 43-year-old man to deceive a 48-year-old man by falsely claiming they could facilitate the purchase of a used Honda CR-V, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit, for RM33,000.
The offence was allegedly committed at a premises here between May 13 and 14.
The charge was framed under Section 109 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 420 of the same Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 12 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane for the offence.

The couple was also jointly charged with deceiving a 43-year-old woman by claiming they could facilitate the purchase of a used Lexus RX350, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit, for RM40,000.
The offence, framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, was allegedly committed at a premises in Taman Sri Andalas here between April 13 and 14.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 15 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane for the offence.
According to the case facts, the male victim met the couple at a restaurant to obtain information about the sale of used vehicles in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit.
During the meeting, Al Zulfadly introduced himself as an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor and claimed he could arrange the purchase of vehicles through an auction.
He allegedly used his purported position to convince both victims that he could secure vehicles for them at lower prices.
Believing his claims, the victims transferred RM33,000 and RM40,000, respectively, into a bank account belonging to Al Zulfadly. However, neither received the vehicles as promised.

Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Amirah Zahari urged the court to order the prison terms to run consecutively, citing the seriousness of the offences, particularly the impersonation of an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor.

“The accused deceived two complainants, who believed he possessed the influence to facilitate the purchase of vehicles. This severe sentence serves as a clear message to the public that the court views such offences with the utmost seriousness and will not compromise with those who break the law.
“It is also hoped that this sentence will serve as a lesson to both the accused and the public, as a deterrent against similar offences,” she said.
However, Al Zulfadly’s lawyer, Yong Kum Lam, from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), appealed for a lighter sentence, saying his client was unemployed and remorseful.
The couple was initially charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court on Nov 12 with cheating involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM33,000.
The following day, Nov 13, they were charged at the Klang Magistrate’s Court over the RM40,000 vehicle scam. The case was subsequently transferred to the Shah Alam court.

On Nov 16, Al Zulfadly was sentenced to one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane by the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court after pleading guilty to cheating a celebrity in a property purchase scam.

The following day, he was sentenced by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to two years’ imprisonment and four strokes of the cane after being convicted on four counts of cheating a female doctor of RM155,000 involving property and luxury vehicle purchases. — Bernama

fe954183033f4103: LONDON: British retail sales volumes unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October compared with September, bolstered by a government call for households to stock up on long-life items as well as stronger clothing sales, official figures showed on Friday.
The jump in October sales volumes beat all economists' forecasts in a Reuters poll and lifted the annual growth in sales to a two-month high of 2.3% from 0.4% in September.

"Supermarkets have told us that sales of long-life food items such as tinned food and UHT milk were boosted by the government's 'Be Ready' campaign," Office for National Statistics (ONS) chief economist Grant Fitzner said.
UK households told to keep three days of food and water

Last month, Britain's government advised the public to keep three days of emergency supplies at home, ​a message it said had been hammered home by online computing security flaws, as well as a record-setting summer of heat, drought and wildfires.

Food stores reported a 0.8% rise in sales volumes in October after a 0.3% drop the month before, the ONS said, while cooler weather also boosted sales of autumnal clothes after a warmer than usual September.
There was no immediate market reaction to the data, which retail analysts said shed little light on longer-term trends.
"An unexpected recovery in retail sales in October underlines the current fickle nature of consumer confidence.

"The increase in sales ... is probably a one-off which hides the challenge facing retailers as they head into the crucial festive trading period," said Rajeev Shaunak, head of consumer at accountants MHA.

Consumer sentiment had fallen sharply in October, according to Britain's longest-running measure of it, as rising fuel bills and borrowing costs squeezed households, although November data released earlier on Friday showed a small recovery.

Consumer price inflation rose to a one-year high of 3.6% in October, and the Bank of England forecast it would reach close to 5% in the middle of next year when it raised interest rates for the first time in three years this month.
However, overall economic growth has been stronger than expected this year and recent updates from major British retailers have been mixed.

Clothing and food retailer Marks & Spencer said recent trading had been solid and it entered the Christmas period with momentum, while Primark and Next highlighted a pickup in sales in October when the weather turned colder.

However, JD Sports said its UK sales trend softened in its third quarter versus a soccer World Cup-boosted second quarter, while discounter Poundland considered entering administration, a form of insolvency protection.

e7a9a4d46a3a1c62: JURF AL-SAKHER (Iraq), Nov 20 — Iraqi government forces on Friday entered the main stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hezbollah group, under what appears to be a compromise that would maintain the faction’s presence and avert a confrontation.
An AFP correspondent in Jurf al-Sakher, south of Baghdad, reported seeing police forces pass through the first Kataeb Hezbollah checkpoint, where the group’s fighters remained deployed.

4e0715028a631984: In other countries, local communities have a say in their futures. If the UK were truly democratic, everywhere would be a parish in control of its own fate Poor Piddington. The Oxfordshire village of just 350 people was told last week by the communities secretary, Angela Rayner, that it must almost quadruple in size. That wasn’t all. The newcomers would be 1,250 young asylum seekers, mainly from Afghanistan and Eritrea, victims of Britain’s chaotic asylum appeal system. They will be housed in former military cabins on the village’s outskirts. Rayner said that this was an “urgent crown development”, which allowed her to ignore local objections. And there had certainly been objections. In September, Piddington villagers declared they were fed up with Britain. Led by their parish council and on a 92% turnout, they voted overwhelmingly to leave the UK and become a “principality”. They are joined in their protest by Barnham in Suffolk, where locals have been told this week that they are to host nearly 1,000 asylum seekers. They have set their own date on a referendum to leave the UK. Simon Jenkins is a Guardian columnist, author and BBC broadcaster. His book The Village in Britain: And Why Place Matters is published this month Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? cb6b8f7f209ece1b: HONG KONG, Nov 20 — Tech-rich Seoul, Tokyo and Taipei led losses across Asia on Friday as Anthropic’s sparkling debut failed to muster a recovery in sentiment towards the AI trade, with nerves frayed by worries over crisis-hit Nvidia, profitability and regulation.
After its record-breaking initial public offering, Claude-creator Anthropic soared 17 per cent on its first day as ordinary investors sought to grab a piece of the new kid on the block.
But the rally did nothing to drag other, more established firms higher as the uncertainty that has hung over the tech sector in recent months sapped confidence, sending Wall Street deep into the red.

Magnificent Seven members who led a scorching surge over the past two years continued a retreat that has characterised trade since the summer, as investors fret over AI profitability, eye-watering spending, rising borrowing costs and geopolitics.

Microsoft, Apple, Amazon and Tesla were all well down, along with Nvidia — which is battling to deal with the fallout from a spy scandal that has led to the resignation of pivotal leader Jensen Huang.
The losses continued on US futures markets, with Anthropic dropping more than four per cent.

Traders have also been spooked by the US Commerce Department’s move to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia’s powerful AI chips remotely, adding to worries that a new Democratic-led Congress will impose further regulations.
The selling followed through to Asia, where Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei — home to the region’s leading AI-linked firms — tumbled between five and 6.2 per cent.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 was dragged by losses of 11 per cent in Kioxia and 14.5 per cent in tech investor SoftBank, while TSMC shed 4.8 per cent and MediaTek tanked 10 per cent as Taiwan’s main stock market was dragged more than six per cent lower.
SK hynix and Samsung took the brunt as South Korea’s Kospi dived more than five per cent.
Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Bangkok, Jakarta and Manila also took a pummelling.
London, Paris and Frankfurt extended the losses at the open.
The flight from risk boosted the safe-haven yen, helped by a surge in Japanese inflation last month that stoked bets on another central bank interest rate hike.
US Treasuries were also boosted, with yields on most term-lengths dropping. Yields fall as demand sends prices higher.

“With volatility elevated, equity futures breaking support and high-beta assets under pressure, traders will increasingly look for signs of capitulation, stabilisation or a catalyst capable of reversing sentiment,” said Chris Weston at Pepperstone.
“The risk is that selling becomes self-reinforcing. As volatility rises, risk limits tighten, leveraged positions are reduced and systematic strategies can add to the pressure.

“Whether Anthropic’s IPO proves to be a defining moment for the AI trade remains to be seen. For now, the immediate priority is watching how markets settle into the weekend and whether buyers can regain control next week.”

Investors are keeping tabs on developments in the Nvidia case as California announced it was investigating whether the firm misled the public and investors about its chips ending up in China, despite federal export controls.
Huang resigned last week after reports alleged he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman named Alice Huang who is a suspected Chinese spy.

Alice Huang, who is no relation, is the former director of Megaspeed, a cloud computing company based in Singapore that was investigated by local officials in 2025 over potential export control violations.
Jensen Huang has agreed to attend a closed-door questioning session about national security issues with Congressional officials on December 1.

Oil prices rose on worries about fresh violence in the Middle East and after the International Energy Agency (IEA) said the crisis in the Middle East had created the “largest threat” to energy security in history.
The IEA said in its annual World Energy Outlook that consumers were increasingly footing the bill as the world runs out of ways to absorb the impact of the conflict on energy supplies. — AFP
9e62b9369a0c2c69: KYIV, Nov 20 — Russia pummelled Ukraine with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight in a massive attack hours after President Vladimir Putin had vowed a “painful” response for Kyiv’s strikes on the Crimean bridge this week.
At least three people were killed in Kyiv and another two in Lviv, power was knocked out in parts of the capital and vital transport bridges were hit, officials said.

The deadly strikes came after Putin met China’s Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in China, where the Russian leader had touted the three men’s “shared responsibility” for global security and issued a joint “declaration toward peace” that made no mention of Moscow’s almost five-year invasion of Ukraine.
AFP journalists saw people hunkering in Kyiv’s metro stations — which double as overnight air-raid shelters — sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents.
Explosions rang out through the night and unofficial monitoring services reported up to three dozen missiles in Ukraine’s air space at one point in the night.
“At present, 3 people are known to have been killed,” Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko wrote on Telegram on Friday.
At least another 15 were reported wounded, he said.
Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were also hit, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city.
And two people were killed at a commuter train station on the outskirts of the western city of Lviv, the governor said.
Russia has intensified its targeting of Kyiv over the last six months and ahead of what many fear will be the toughest winter of the war.

Attacks throughout the day on Thursday — while the summit in China was underway and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met his European backers in Berlin — had damaged a landmark cathedral and embassies of foreign countries.
The Austrian, Brazilian and Dutch embassies saw light damage after volleys of drones were fired on Kyiv in an hours-long barrage on the city centre.

Russia’s military on Friday morning confirmed it had launched a “massive” attack with missiles and drones, saying they targeted military-industrial sites and transport infrastructure in several regions, including bridges in Kyiv.
Bridge retaliation
Speaking in China after meeting Trump and Xi, Putin had vowed no let-up in Russia’s assaults on Ukraine.
The war, unleashed with his 2022 invasion, has killed hundreds of thousands and forced millions to flee their homes in eastern and southern Ukraine.
He had said Russia’s response to Ukraine’s strikes on a bridge linking Russia to the annexed Crimean peninsula would be “much more painful”.
Ukrainian attacks earlier this week severed the highway of the road-and-rail link in two, according to satellite images published by the Vantor imaging firm.
The multi-billion-dollar 19-kilometre (12-mile) bridge is a symbol of Russia’s annexation of the peninsula and has been a target for Ukraine throughout the war.
One more person was killed in Ukraine’s southern Zaporizhzhia region in the overnight attacks, while a hospital was hit in the northeastern city of Kharkiv, officials said.
Russia’s defence ministry said it had intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones fired at the country, while Moscow-installed officials in occupied eastern Ukraine reported three people killed there.
Moscow invite
US-led talks on ending the fighting have so far shown little signs of progress, with Moscow having stuck to its hardline demands.
Putin has said any deal to end the war in Ukraine must be part of a wider agreement on European security.
Speaking in China on Thursday, he said any form of Ukraine-Europe military cooperation as part of that deal would be a “problem.”
He has also so far refused to let European representatives join the US-led talks with Ukraine.
Putin said Russia had invited Europeans to Moscow to discuss their position, before he would decide if they should join the negotiations.
He did not say who he had invited.
In Berlin, Zelensky said it would be a “mistake” for Europeans to travel to Moscow for the talks, but has urged them to be included in the negotiations taking place in third countries.
European leaders have pushed back against Putin’s calls to reshape European security, with the Russian leader seeking a massive roll-back of NATO forces in eastern and central Europe.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted on Thursday that Europe will have a seat at the table at talks that should “take place soon”. — AFP
